newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: AIR BOTSWANA SEES PRIVATISATION GO-AHEAD IN AUGUST.
newsitem.headline: AIR BOTSWANA SEES PRIVATISATION GO-AHEAD IN AUGUST.

text.p: Air Botswana's general manager Joshua Galeforolwe said on Monday he expected the airline to be given the green light for privatisation in August.
"We were told by the government that as soon as we become profitable, we would be privatised," Galeforolwe told Reuters.
"At the end of March, we recorded the first net profit ever in Air Botswana since it was formed in 1965," he added, saying details of the audited results would be released next month.
Galeforolwe, who had helped to turn the airline around from a 20 million pula loss three years ago, said a privatisation plan for Air Botswana was ready to be submitted.
"We have been talking to many parties, including the International Finance Corporation (IFC). They have made us a proposal which we are taking up with government," he said.
Privatisation was was likely to take up to three years.
"The programme we envisage would take at least 12 months without any delays, but there will have to be a lot of legislative issues," he said.
"Nothing will have happened by the time we give out next year's accounts, so we should be able to show two years of continuous profit and prove we are a bankable proposition."
Galeforolwe said the airline was aiming for partial privatisation as air agreements with other countries specified that the carrier be controlled by Botswana nationals.
"Our view is that we need a strong partner which flies from the regional hub (in South Africa) and to whom we can feed traffic," he said

The airline is targetting flights to Zambia, Zimbabwe, Uganda and Tanzania. Its core route is a return flight from the capital Gaborone to Johannesburg, while it also has flights to Harare in Zimbabwe.
Traffic is mainly geared towards businesspeople and feeder traffic to Johannesburg's international airport. Tourism makes up a small percentage of Air Botswana.
"Our growth is mainly business traffic. It is high yield... less price sensitive and non-seasonal," Galeforolwe said.
